title: Korea Exchange Bank public shareholdings → Lone Star Funds
summary: Korea Exchange Bank (KEB) was partly privatized in 1989 with the government keeping 51%; Commerzbank became a large shareholder in 1998 and the state-run Export-Import Bank of Korea (KEXIM) held a stake. On 27 August 2003 Lone Star Funds agreed to acquire 51% of KEB for 1.38 trillion won through a new share issue plus shares sold by Commerzbank and KEXIM; regulators approved in September 2003. Lone Star bought more shares from the two in 2006, was ordered by the FSC in 2011 to cut its 51.02% stake, and sold to Hana Financial Group in February 2012 (4.4 trillion won including KEXIM's shares). Korean courts tried the KEB Card share-price case and cleared a finance-ministry official accused of lowering the sale price. An ICSID award of US$216.5 million against Korea (2022) was annulled in full in November 2025.

claims.claim: Lone Star acquired Korea Exchange Bank at 10-20 cents on the dollar.
claims.explanation: Lone Star paid 1.38 trillion won for 51%, part of it as new capital into the bank. No source retrieved gives KEB's book value or a price-to-book ratio. Prosecutors alleged a former finance-ministry official conspired to lower the price by up to 825 billion won below fair market value; in November 2008 a Korean court cleared him, saying it could not judge that the capital-ratio estimate had been manipulated to lower the price or to make Lone Star eligible. A 2022 ICSID tribunal later found Korea liable only for delaying the 2012 sale approval, and that award was annulled in 2025.

claims.claim: Korea Exchange Bank was a Tier-1 national bank.
claims.explanation: The Korea Times described KEB as the country's fifth-largest lender in 2008 and again in 2011. It was a nationwide commercial bank, but the 2003 purchase was structured around an assessment that the bank's capital ratio was below the threshold that would otherwise have barred a non-financial buyer, and the Korea Times called it 'then-fragile'. 'Tier-1' is not a term the sources use.

claims.claim: Lone Star bought a bank that had been recapitalized on the backs of Korean taxpayers.
claims.explanation: Korea committed 168.7 trillion won of public funds to its financial sector after 1997 (about half through the KDIC for deposits and recapitalization, a quarter through KAMCO for bad loans), and had recovered 72.5% by the time of the FSC report cited. But no source retrieved shows a KDIC or KAMCO injection into KEB before 2003; the sources describe Commerzbank's 1998 investment and Lone Star's own 2003 new-share injection as KEB's recapitalizations. The system-wide figure does not establish the claim for KEB.

claims.claim: Lone Star manipulated KEB Card's share price in 2003 to absorb it cheaply.
claims.explanation: The Seoul Central District Court convicted Paul Yoo, Lone Star and KEB on 1 February 2008; the Seoul High Court acquitted on the manipulation charge on 24 June 2008; the Supreme Court reversed that acquittal on 10 March 2011 and remanded; on retrial in October 2011 the High Court sentenced Yoo to three years and ordered Lone Star to pay 25 billion won, and Yoo appealed again. The outcome of that final appeal is not recorded here.
